title: Contextual Handoff Orchestrator with Split-Window Fidelity Checks
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a contextual handoff orchestrator to improve safe traffic promotions by validating fidelity across short sliding windows; no user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: production rollouts previously used coarse-grained snapshot checks that could miss short-lived fidelity degradations when shadow traffic or minibatches exercised rare model paths. This PR introduces a new Contextual Handoff Orchestrator that performs split-window fidelity checks across multiple telemetry slices before promoting shadow or canary traffic. The goal is to reduce noisy rollbacks while catching regressions that only appear under specific session contexts or short time horizons. Design summary: the orchestrator maintains time-decayed aggregators keyed by configurable context fingerprints (route, session-anchored cohort, device class). For each candidate promote attempt the controller creates N overlapping windows (default N=3) with staggered lengths, computes per-window fidelity signals including latency p95, downstream error rate, and a quality delta compared to baseline via eval hooks, and applies a conjunctive policy: a promotion is allowed only if all windows stay within configured tolerances. There are also soft-promote steps that require two consecutive clean windows for higher-traffic lanes. The controller integrates with the rollback advisor to suggest immediate journaled reverts when a late negative drift is observed. This PR also adds a telemetry slicer that materializes sample-level fingerprints for efficient streaming aggregation, and a bounded replay buffer to support fast bisecting of failing windows. Commits summary: 1) orchestration core and small policy DSL; 2) telemetry slicer and windowed aggregators; 3) console UI and rollout API additions; 4) integration tests, k8s CRD and docs. High-level changed areas: rollout/controller.py, rollout/policies.py, runtime/handshake.go, telemetry/slicer.py, telemetry/window_aggregator.py, console/src/rollouts/handshake-ui.tsx, api/handlers/rollout_v2.go, k8s/handshake-crd.yaml, tests/integration/test_handoff_scenarios.py, docs/handovers.md, ci/pipeline-rollout.yml. Backwards compatibility: rollout API is additive and gated behind a feature flag. Testing: unit tests for aggregator correctness, nightly integration smoke tests emulating bursty traffic, and a perf-canary lab run. Results: perf-canary showed a 42 percent reduction in false-positive rollbacks for transient synthetic noise and surface-detected a regression that only manifested in the 30s window. Key trade-offs and mitigations: cardinality pressure was raised in review; mitigations include a configurable sampling cap, a budget-aware summarizer that prioritizes high-traffic contexts, and a bloom-based prefilter to reduce aggregator load. Metrics added: window_pass_rate, context_cardinality_estimate, sampling_drop_rate, window_fail_timestamps. Ops plan: rollout behind a flag, staged enablement across accounts with 48 hour watch window and automatic fallback to baseline if window_fail_rate exceeds threshold. Known limitations: very high-cardinality contexts can still see sampling drop; recommend coarse fingerprinting or aggregating at route-level if observed. Merge: required two approvals and passing CI; squashed and merged. Post-merge: infra will run a controlled rollout and add dashboard panels for SREs and product owners. Documentation: docs/handovers.md contains playbook, failure modes, and troubleshooting steps.
